1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.

1	# Art Direction for Aura3D Agents
2	
3	Version: 4.0.0 (supersedes `cinematic-scene-quality.md`)
4	
5	Every scene an agent ships has a look: an environment, a key light, a shadow,
6	a background, fog, a grade. This doc is the API-level companion to the
7	`aura3d-art-direction` skill — the skill owns the process, this doc owns the
8	values.
9	
10	## The look does the work
11	
12	A look preset supplies, as one unit:
13	
14	- image-based environment light and reflections (IBL),
15	- a key light at a defined elevation/azimuth with full-strength shadows,
16	- a background (sky, backdrop or declared void),
17	- fog / atmosphere tuned to the palette,
18	- an output post grade (`output.preset`),
19	- DPR and quality caps (`looks.appOptions`).
20	
21	```ts
22	import { createAuraApp, looks, model, scene } from "@aura3d/engine";
23	import { assets } from "./aura-assets";
24	
25	createAuraApp("#app", {
26	  scene: scene().add(looks.preset("product-studio")).add(model(assets.product)),
27	  ...looks.appOptions("product-studio")
28	});
29	```
30

33	Pick the row by genre, then read the full table in

For rocks, I'll just use squashed spheres rather than introducing polyhedrons. The ground will be a horizontal plane scaled to the world dimensions with shadow receiving enabled. The forest is a 180×180 ground plane plus exactly 10,000 instanced objects: 8,000 trees (trunks and canopies) and 2,000 rocks. They come from three instanced nodes (cylinder trunks, cone canopies, sphere rocks), plus the one plane, so no per-object meshes. Placement uses a seeded mulberry32 generator (fixed seed) over a 50 m radius disc, so the forest is the same on every load. Each trunk, canopy and rock gets its own hex colour (browns, greens with some yellow tints, grey stones). The scene has one shadow-casting directional light, a neutral environment for fill, and exponential-squared fog (`effects.fog`, density 0.0045) matching the background colour. The engine's orbit camera mode doesn't move on its own, so each frame an `app.onFrame` callback calls `app.camera.setPose` to move the camera in a slow circle of radius 88 and height 56 (about 105 s per revolution). The framing is meant to keep the whole disc in view. The canvas is used as-is (`resize: false`, `pixelRatio: 1`). `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after the first frames have been drawn, and the engine's own `requestAnimationFrame` loop keeps rendering after that.
